# Batocera `_info.txt` fixtures

These files are **derived from official Batocera generator source**, not
extracted from a Batocera distribution image. Do not describe them as
byte-level image samples.

## `batocera-43.1-nes_info.txt`

- Source tag: `batocera-43.1`
- Source commit: `155c2d8d304cbb53db52e9479dcf683392821d5c` (2026-05-29)
- Generator: `python-src/batocera-es-system/batocera_es_system/roms.py`
  - SHA-256: `d8ce736b6b1337a50e1a52c731e3cf184cdbf56cdc68af56f023e4c0338ad753`
- Metadata: `package/batocera/emulationstation/batocera-es-system/es_systems.yml`
  - SHA-256: `9c8a7b877d77c84e11d647248608f3adb4b031a5d40d8ac0cfb0ec52e6b3f0f6`
  - NES `extensions`: `[nes, unif, unf, zip, 7z]`
  - NES comments: `For more info: …` and `Trouvez la documentation ici: …`
- Generation: invoked the unmodified 43.1 `roms.py` `build()` function with
  the NES name, extension list, and comments above.
- The fixture deliberately preserves the 43.1 generator's behavior of
  concatenating the comment directly after the extension list's closing
  quote. There is no inserted newline before the comment. Trailing blank lines
  are also part of the generated bytes; do not normalize them.
- Fixture SHA-256:
  `3948e67bf34333694cdca81f693bb7ac026f5d6c3010e7abdbf00ab32a958729`

## `batocera-master-multiline-nes_info.txt`

- Same source commit and generator SHA-256 as above.
- Generation: invoked the unmodified master `build()` function with a
  representative `libretro` metadata block containing `fceumm`, `nestopia`,
  and `mesen`, each using the official NES extension set.
- This fixture exercises the master `- emulator/core: extension-list` layout.
  It is not claimed to be byte-identical to any released Batocera 44 image.

## Parser contract exercised by these files

- English section first; French section only as fallback.
- 43.1 quoted inline values may have the comment concatenated after the
  closing quote.
- Master values may be unquoted inline values or contiguous
  `- name: extension-list` core lines.
- Extension names are normalized to lowercase, must begin with `.`, are
  deduplicated, and are sorted by the parser.
- Comments, separators, and other prose are never treated as extensions.
